C0.quote: We characterize all voting rules that satisfy false-name-proofness, strategy-proofness, and ontoness
C0.note: Axiomatic and strategic analysis of voting rules

C1.quote: false-name-proof, strategy-proof, and onto if and only f is a voting by quota
C1.note: Characterization via axioms including strategy-proofness and false-name-proofness (SB properties).

C2.1.quote: mapping profiles of voters’ preferences into social alternatives

C2.2.quote: We assume that Pi is a strict linear order
C2.2.note: Strict linear orders over subsets of objects (separable preferences); not rankings over candidates in the usual sense, so coded OTH.

C2.3.quote: since individual preferences are private information
C2.3.note: True preferences exist separately from reports.

C2.4.quote: voters may behave strategically by not submitting their preferences truthfully
C2.4.note: Strategy-proofness definition uses Pi and Pi' separately.

C3.1.quote: no voter benefits by not revealing their preferences truthfully
C3.1.note: Strategy-proofness considers misreports; false-name-proofness considers repeating the same vote, with no misreporting; the characterization combines both.

C3.2.note: In the false-name analysis voters repeat their own vote, but no statement about sincerity for non-strategic analyses was found.

C4.1.note: Input is not among the listed formats; additive utility representation only used as a preference class, not a welfare notion.

C5.1.note: No welfare or efficiency criteria in results; only axiomatic properties.
